title: Determination of Enzyme Activity
author: Tjusls China
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6gthbwn
materials: Infinite M1000 Pro Automatic Microplate Reader

When the facility ends testing, save data and import it into GraphPad Prism Software. Use “nonlinear fit” – “straight line” to calculate the initial velocity of each reaction a.k.a. its slope value. Choose the condition with higher initial velocity.

steps.title: Clean and dry plates
steps.instruction: Soak the 96‑well plates in 75 % ethanol, place the container in an ultrasonic cleaner for 30 min to 1 h, wash the plates several times with ddH₂O, then dry them in a drying oven at 55 °C.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the enzyme stock with its buffer: pipette 1 µL protein stock into 1 mL buffer and mix gently; then perform a 5‑fold serial dilution by pipetting 100 µL of the previous protein solution into 400 µL fresh buffer each step.

steps.title: Load reaction wells
steps.instruction: Pipette 94 µL protein solution into nine wells (typically B2‑D4) to create three parallel experimental replicates; pipette 94 µL buffer without protein into three wells as negative controls; finally add 6 µL fluorescent substrate to each well.

steps.title: Program microplate reader
steps.instruction: Set up the Infinite M1000 Pro program: shake the plate for 10 s at 654 rpm, then run a kinetic fluorescence read with 75 cycles, each cycle lasting 10 s.

steps.title: Run fluorescence measurement
steps.instruction: Place the prepared plate into the Infinite M1000 Pro reader and press the Start button to begin the kinetic run.

steps.title: Select linear fluorescence range
steps.instruction: After the run, save the data, import it into GraphPad Prism, apply a “nonlinear fit → straight line” to each concentration, and compare the R² values; keep the concentration series whose line has an R² closest to 1 as the linear range.

steps.title: Create enzyme concentration gradient
steps.instruction: Using the selected standard concentration, prepare parallel dilutions at 2×, 0.5×, 0.25×, etc., then repeat steps 3‑5 for each new concentration.

steps.title: Calculate emission ratio and EC80
steps.instruction: For each reaction, compute rE = Q₀ / Qₘ (Q₀ = maximum fluorescence of that reaction, Qₘ = maximum fluorescence among all reactions). In GraphPad Prism, set log(protein concentration) as X and rE as Y, choose “nonlinear fit → log(agonist) vs. response – Find ECanything”, and enter 80 as the F‑parameter to obtain the EC₈₀ value.

steps.title: Set protein to EC80 concentration
steps.instruction: Adjust the protein solution to the EC₈₀ concentration (or a nearby value if experimental conditions require) for subsequent assays.

steps.title: Measure at EC80
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 3‑5 using the EC₈₀ protein concentration to collect kinetic data.

steps.title: Dilute protein with optimal buffer
steps.instruction: If needed, dilute the protein again with the most suitable buffer solution to reach the desired final concentration.

steps.title: Prepare substrate dilution series
steps.instruction: Dilute the fluorescent substrate in a 2‑fold series to generate eight concentration groups, then repeat steps 3‑5 for each substrate concentration.

steps.title: Determine initial velocities
steps.instruction: Save each kinetic run, import the data into GraphPad Prism, and apply a “nonlinear fit → straight line” to obtain the slope (initial velocity) of each reaction.

steps.title: Fit Michaelis‑Menten curve
steps.instruction: Using the initial velocities and corresponding substrate concentrations, choose “nonlinear fit → Michaelis‑Menten” in GraphPad Prism; the software will output Km and Vmax automatically.

steps.title: Calibrate fluorescence response
steps.instruction: Dilute protein in a 2‑fold series for several groups, repeat steps 3‑5, then plot fluorescence intensity (FI) as Y versus substrate concentration [S] as X and fit a straight line to obtain the fluorescence calibration factor.

steps.title: Calculate kcat
steps.instruction: Compute kcat using the equation kcat = Vmax / [E], where [E] is the enzyme concentration used in the Michaelis‑Menten assay.
